question: Recall that the conjugate of the complex number \(w = a + bi,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are real numbers and \(i = \sqrt{-1},\) is the complex number \(\overline{w} = a - bi.\) For any complex number \(z,\) let \(f(z) = 4i\overline{z}.\) The polynomial \[ P(z) = z^4 + 4z^3 + 3z^2 + 2z + 1 \] has four complex roots: \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(z_3,\) and \(z_4.\) Let \[ \begin{aligned} &Q(z) = z^4 + Az^3 + Bz^2 \\ &\quad {}+ Cz + D \end{aligned} \] be the polynomial whose roots are \(f(z_1),\) \(f(z_2),\) \(f(z_3),\) and \(f(z_4),\) where the coefficients \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) and \(D\) are complex numbers. What is \(B + D?\)
solution:
The coefficients \(B\) and \(D\) depend only on pairwise products and the product of all four roots, so there is no need to find the roots individually.

Expanding \(P(t)=\prod_{j=1}^4(t-z_j)\) shows that the coefficient of \(t^2\) is the sum of all six pairwise root products, while the constant term is the product of all four roots. Both signs are positive because these terms select an even number of negative root factors. Thus
\[
\sum_{1\le r<s\le4}z_rz_s=3,
\qquad z_1z_2z_3z_4=1.
\]
Conjugation preserves sums and products:
\[
\overline{u+v}=\overline u+\overline v,
\qquad \overline{uv}=\overline u\,\overline v.
\]
These identities follow by writing the complex numbers in real and imaginary parts.

The roots of \(Q\) are \(4i\overline{z_j}\). Each pairwise product therefore acquires a factor \((4i)^2=-16\), giving
\[
B=(4i)^2\overline{\sum_{r<s}z_rz_s}
=-16\overline3=-48.
\]
The product of all four transformed roots acquires a factor \((4i)^4=256\), so
\[
D=(4i)^4\overline{z_1z_2z_3z_4}
=256\overline1=256.
\]
Consequently,
\[
B+D=-48+256=\boxed{208},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Because \(P\) has real coefficients, conjugating all its roots leaves its factorization unchanged. This lets us build \(Q\) by substitution.

Indeed, conjugation preserves sums and products, and the coefficients of \(P\) are real. Hence
\[
P(t)=\overline{P(\overline t)}
=\overline{\prod_{j=1}^4(\overline t-z_j)}
=\prod_{j=1}^4(t-\overline{z_j}).
\]
This identity includes all roots with their multiplicities. It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q(t)
&=\prod_{j=1}^4(t-4i\overline{z_j})\\
&=(4i)^4\prod_{j=1}^4\left(\frac{t}{4i}-\overline{z_j}\right)\\
&=(4i)^4P\left(\frac{t}{4i}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substituting into the given polynomial gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
Q(t)
&=t^4+4(4i)t^3+3(4i)^2t^2+2(4i)^3t+(4i)^4\\
&=t^4+16it^3-48t^2-128it+256.
\end{aligned}
\]
Reading off the requested coefficients,
\[
B+D=-48+256=\boxed{208},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Transform the whole polynomial
